To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have experimentally demonstrated a new type of three-wave resonant interaction, the so-called forced interaction, which can occur in systems with significant dissipation.

(1) we show that the generation of a wave by the three-wave interaction mechanism does not necessarily follow the dispersion relation; (2) the bandwidth of the transfer function of the surface is increased by dissipation; (3) we propose a model of the free surface response at lowest order in the nonlinear regime; (4) we show that this model can explain the generation of waves that do not verify the dispersion relation; and (5) we discuss the consequences of this mechanism for wave turbulence
the viscous dissipated energy of capillary surface waves can be used to excite daughter waves that do not verify the linear dispersion relation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the dynamics of nonlinear wave systems, with a focus on capillary-gravity water waves, and more recently with the study of nonlinear wave systems in the presence of a magnetic field.
the interaction of capillary-gravitational surface waves in a viscous fluid.
the study of surface waves.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the nonlinear interaction between three capillary-gravity waves is not a pure resonant interaction.
three-wave interactions are the main mechanism for wave energy exchanges in a capillary-gravity fluid, even if some of the daughter waves do not verify the dispersion relation.
the nonlinear interactions of capillary surface waves are not only governed by three-wave resonances but also by three-wave forced interactions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the three-wave resonant interactions can be divided into two categories: one with the daughter wave satisfying the dispersion relation and the other with the daughter wave not satisfying the dispersion relation.
three-wave resonant interaction is a necessary but not sufficient condition to generate a daughter wave.

the three-wave resonant interactions are not the only mechanism for the wave turbulence, and the viscous dissipated wave turbulence is possible in some systems with the forced three-wave interactions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the viscous damping can be so important that the linear dispersion relation can be violated.
three-wave resonant interactions do not always lead to the generation of waves satisfying the linear dispersion relation.
the nonlinear interactions between waves in a fluid can be significantly modified by the presence of dissipation.
